summary: Stone lookout on Flagg Mountain built by the CCC in 1935; staffed until 1989, closed to the public for 20-plus years, and reopened in June 2022 with renovated stairs.

facts.design: 50-foot stone tower with walls 2 to 3 feet thick and a 12-by-12-foot cab; criss-cross timbers replaced with inlaid stone

access.note: The Alabama Trails Foundation says the tower area is open to the public for picnics and invites climbing the renovated stairs; a 2017 register visit had found the stairs unsafe.

visit.trail_note: Alabama Trails Foundation invites visitors to climb the renovated stairs to the cab; Flagg Mountain marks the start of the Alabama Pinhoti Trail

events.note: Built by the Civilian Conservation Corps (CCC)
The Alabama Forestry Commission staffed the cab until 1989
NHLR visit report: stairs not safe; not staffed; full-time caretaker living on site
As of 2019 several CCC-era cabins were being renovated and were available for overnight rental
Tower reopened to the public in June 2022 after more than four years of work by the Alabama Hiking Trail Society and partners; the stairs were renovated

resolved_conflicts.explanation: A 2017 NHLR visit report says the lookout stairs are not safe; the Alabama Trails Foundation later calls them newly renovated. The later description is used for current visiting, and the 2017 report is dated.

sources.title: Flagg's historic fire tower reopened to public
Welcome to Flagg Mountain, Alabama's first mountain!

notes_for_editor: The 2022 reopening year comes from the Coosa County News web address (2022/06/24); the article body says June 15 without a year. height_m 15.2 is converted from the register's 50-foot figure. Staffing is recorded as unstaffed as of 2017; the register notes a full-time caretaker on site then, and a later caretaker is mentioned in the 2022 article without a date. The register lists elevation 1,104 ft; a Wikidata entry gives 1,142 ft and spells the name 'Flag Mountain'; not used. An al.com 2011 article was blocked (HTTP 403) and was not read. The Alabama Living magazine article on issuu was not readable. The NHLR is the only source for the 1989 staffing end date.
